reason: The same name is the highest for Nāths, Nirañjanīs and Dādū, and a lower, deceiving power for the Kabīr Panth and Sant Mat; see dsp:status-of-niranjan.
Sant Mat itself identifies Sat Lok with Sach Khand.
Same name as the Purāṇic highest world of Brahmā, but the Kabīr Panth places Satlok beyond all worlds of Kāl, including Brahmā's.
Sant Mat's surat is the individual soul considered as a current of attention.
Both name an opening at the crown; the Sant Mat Daswān Dwār is a region, not only an aperture.
Both name the highest centre in the head; the Sant image is not systematized as a lotus.
Located at the brow like the ājñā cakra, but Sant Mat places it above the six lower cakras as the door out of the body.
Both are coded, paradoxical registers; the Sant form is a genre of songs, the Buddhist/Bāul form a language of double meanings.
Both describe freedom in the living body; the Sant term stresses the death of the self rather than the dawning of knowledge.
The Sant satguru is the guru who reveals the Name within; outward family or sect gurus are not satgurus.
The Bāul maner mānuṣ and the Sahajiyā sahaja mānuṣa name the same indwelling divine person in the two idioms.
Like perception, bartamān is direct knowledge, but it is specifically the body's own experience and is set against scripture as such.
Both describe an upward reversal of the vital substance; the Bāul form is a couple's practice and is framed devotionally.
The Sant 'Lord within' and the Bāul 'Man of the Heart' are the indwelling divine in two idioms (P3-path); the Bāuls stress the body and the living human, the Sants the Name.
Bāul and Sahajiyā names of the same indwelling Man.
The haṭha and Nāth idea of the upward-turned seed, in a devotional and couple-based frame; the Bāuls would not accept a purely yogic reading.
The Sant jīvan-mṛtak and sahaj correspond to liberation while living; the Kabīr Panth and Sant Mat add a post-mortem return to Satlok/Sach Khand.
The Sant upside-down song and the Bengali coded song share the device of paradox that hides and reveals.
Both make sound/word the ultimate's own power; the Sant Word is heard within and is not the Veda (which Sant Mat places at Trikuṭī).
Both teach absorption through successive inner sounds; the Sant Mat sounds are assigned to regions and the goal is beyond sound.
Name-repetition, but the Sants stress the inward, mind-held remembrance over counted recitation.
Both are absorption in the inner sound; surat-śabd yoga adds the master's form, the names and the regional cosmology.
The Sant critique targets all sectarian garb, not only false ascetics.
Five of the six enemies (envy omitted).
Pride of family/lineage; the Sant critique extends to the whole caste order.
